prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single, universally “best” roofing company for every homeowner — the right choice depends on your location in Dallas, roof type, budget, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and whether you prioritize speed, price, or long-term warranties.

If you want, I can pull a short, vetted list of top roofers near you — tell me your ZIP code and any special requirements (shingle vs. metal/tile, insurance claim, timing). In the meantime, here’s a quick guide so you can find and vet the best roofer for your job.

How to pick the best roofer for your Dallas roof replacement
- Get multiple quotes: 3 written estimates so you can compare scope and materials, not just price.
- Verify credentials:
  - Check contractor registration with the City of Dallas (some cities require registration) and local permits.
  - Confirm general liability and workers’ comp insurance — get certificate of insurance and call the carrier to verify.
  - Look for manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) if you want a superior shingle warranty.
- Check reputation:
  - Read recent Google, Yelp, and Facebook reviews and ask for at least 3 local references or examples of recent jobs.
  - Check Better Business Bureau for complaints and handling.
- Warranty & workmanship:
  - Ask about both manufacturer shingle warranty and the contractor’s workmanship warranty (length and what’s covered).
  - Find out who handles warranty callbacks and what the process is.
- Contract & payment:
  - Get a detailed written contract: scope, materials (brand & class), tear-off vs. overlay, disposal, timeline, payment schedule, change order process.
  - Avoid large up-front cash-only payments. Typical deposit is limited; final payment after inspection and lien release/paid invoices from subs.
- Storm/insurance claims:
  - If filing a claim, confirm the roofer will meet with the adjuster and provide a written scope and estimate you can submit.
  - Beware of contractors who pressure you to sign immediately after a storm or offer to waive your deductible.
- Red flags:
  - No physical address or local presence, no insurance proof, high-pressure sales tactics, only takes cash, extremely low bid compared to others, vague contract terms.

Sample questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed/registered with the City of Dallas? Can you provide the registration number?
- Are you certified by any shingle manufacturers? Which ones?
- Can you provide a Certificate of Insurance and list of recent local references?
- What exactly is included (number of layers removed, underlayment type, ventilation, drip-edge, flashing replacement)?
- What warranties do you provide (length and what’s covered)? Who services warranty issues?
- What is the expected start and completion date? How do you handle delays?
- Will you obtain permits and handle inspections?

If you want, give me your ZIP code and any priorities (price, warranty, storm work/insurance claim, roof material) and I’ll compile 3–5 highly rated, vetted roofing companies in your area with summary notes and next steps.
